full.body:
## East side

- **Gorham Mountain Loop:** 3.5 miles, moderate and rocky.
- **Beehive Loop:** 1.4 miles with iron rungs and exposed cliff travel; only in dry conditions.
- **Great Head:** 1.7 miles over rocky coastal terrain.

## Central mountains

- **Jordan Pond Path:** 3.3 miles with boulders and narrow boardwalk on the west side.
- **Pemetic Loop:** 4 miles with scrambling, rungs, and a ladder.
- **Cadillac South Ridge:** 7.1 miles and a substantial exposed ridge day.

## West side and Schoodic

- **Beech Mountain:** 1.2 miles; drive because there is no direct trailhead transit.
- **Ship Harbor:** 1.3-mile easier coastal loop.
- **Schoodic:** choose among 7.5 miles of linked trails.

Routes 4, 5, and 6 do not stop at the Bubble Rock trailhead. Use Jordan Pond for a bus-based approach or drive with a parking backup.

full.body:
The parks are open 24 hours daily and do not require an entrance reservation. "Park access" below describes an unstaffed trail or roadside area, not staffed services or a recommendation to visit outside safe daylight hours.

## Foothills and Generals Highway

| Site or attraction                                                                    | Hours and access                   | Why go and current notes                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Foothills Visitor Center](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/visitorcenters.htm) | Daily 8 am-5 pm                    | Short orientation, conditions, maps, restrooms, and water near the Ash Mountain entrance.                                                             |
| [Hospital Rock](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/driveviewsum.htm)              | Park access; Generals Highway open | Native American pictographs, bedrock mortars, and Kaweah Canyon views. Current fire restrictions prohibit wood and charcoal fires at the picnic area. |
| [Amphitheater Point](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/driveviewsum.htm)         | Park access; roadside pullout      | Quick viewpoint with a side view of Moro Rock and a foothills-to-alpine panorama when visibility is good.                                             |

## Giant Forest

| Site or attraction                                                                           | Hours and access                              | Why go and current notes                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Giant Forest Museum](https://www.nps.gov/seki/learn/historyculture/gfgfm.htm)               | Daily 9 am-5 pm                               | Historic museum interpreting sequoias, meadows, and human history. Start here before Big Trees Trail.                                                                         |
| [Big Trees Trail](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/gfdayhikesum.htm)                   | Park access; begin at the museum              | Accessible interpretive circuit around Round Meadow, approximately 0.75-1 mile. Allow about one hour.                                                                         |
| [General Sherman Tree and Congress Trail](https://www.nps.gov/seki/learn/nature/sherman.htm) | Park access; main lot and Wolverton Road open | Highest-priority grove experience. The main approach descends a half mile; one Congress Trail section is under reconstruction through September, so confirm the signed route. |
| [Moro Rock](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/gfdayhikesum.htm)                         | Park access; Moro Rock Loop open              | Stair climb gaining about 300 feet to Great Western Divide views. Avoid rain, ice, lightning, and poor visibility.                                                            |
| [Tunnel Log and Crescent Meadow](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/driveviewsum.htm)    | Park access; Crescent Meadow Road open        | Combine the quick Tunnel Log photo stop with the meadow and nearby sequoia trails.                                                                                            |
| [Beetle Rock](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/driveviewsum.htm)                       | Park access; short walk from the museum       | Broad granite viewpoint and an easy addition before or after the museum.                                                                                                      |

## Grant Grove

| Site or attraction                                                      | Hours and access                             | Why go and current notes                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Kings Canyon Visitor Center](https://www.nps.gov/seki/grant-grove.htm) | Daily 8 am-5 pm                              | The visitor center at Grant Grove. Confirm Highway 180 and Cedar Grove conditions before the canyon drive. |
| [General Grant Tree](https://www.nps.gov/seki/learn/nature/grant.htm)   | Park access; Grant Grove trails open         | Paved one-third-mile loop with the General Grant Tree, Gamlin Cabin, Fallen Monarch, and Centennial Stump. |
| [Panoramic Point](https://www.nps.gov/seki/grant-grove.htm)             | Park access; road open to passenger vehicles | Views across Kings Canyon and Hume Lake. The road is narrow and prohibits motor homes and trailers.        |

## Kings Canyon Scenic Byway and Cedar Grove

| Site or attraction                                                                                     | Hours and access                       | Why go and current notes                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Kings Canyon Scenic Byway](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/byways.htm)                         | Highway 180 open to Roads End          | Dedicated driving day. Allow 45-60 minutes each way just for the Grant Grove-to-Cedar Grove descent, before stops.           |
| [Junction View, Yucca Point, and Canyon View](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/driveviewsum.htm) | Park access; roadside overlooks        | Prioritize Junction View and Canyon View; add Yucca Point if pullout conditions are comfortable.                             |
| [Grizzly Falls](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/driveviewsum.htm)                               | Park access; five-minute roadside walk | Shady, high-value waterfall stop with little time cost.                                                                      |
| [Roaring River Falls](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/cgdayhikesum.htm)                         | Park access; short paved walk          | Granite-chute waterfall three miles east of Cedar Grove Village.                                                             |
| [Zumwalt Meadow](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/cgdayhikesum.htm)                              | Park access; trail reported open       | Approximately 0.8-mile current route with meadow, granite walls, talus, and river views. Flood damage ended the former loop. |
| [Knapp's Cabin](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/cgdayhikesum.htm)                               | Park access; short walk from a turnout | Unusual 1920s fishing-expedition cabin and a quick human-history stop.                                                       |
| [Roads End and Muir Rock](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/driveviewsum.htm)                     | Highway 180 open to the terminus       | Granite-wall views, river access, and a worthwhile finish to the scenic byway when daylight permits.                         |

## Closed or constrained

- **Crystal Cave:** tours have ended for the entire 2026 season. Remove it from the active itinerary.
- **Shuttles:** 2026 summer service ended September 7, and Kings Canyon has no in-park shuttle.
- **Mineral King:** major daytime construction closures make it a poor spontaneous backup.
- **Parking:** General Sherman and Giant Forest Museum lots can fill early, especially on weekends.

Recheck [roads](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/road-conditions.htm), [current conditions](https://www.nps.gov/seki/planyourvisit/conditions.htm), and live alerts each morning.

searchDocuments.body: The parks are open 24 hours daily and do not require an entrance reservation. "Park access" below describes an unstaffed trail or roadside area, not staffed services or a recommendation to visit outside safe daylight hours. Foothills and Generals Highway Site or attraction Hours and access Why go and current notes Foothills Visitor Center Daily 8 am-5 pm Short orientation, conditions, maps, restrooms, and water near the Ash Mountain entrance. Hospital Rock Park access; Generals Highway open Native American pictographs, bedrock mortars, and Kaweah Canyon views. Current fire restrictions prohibit wood and charcoal fires at the picnic area. Amphitheater Point Park access; roadside pullout Quick viewpoint with a side view of Moro Rock and a foothills-to-alpine panorama when visibility is good. Giant Forest Site or attraction Hours and access Why go and current notes Giant Forest Museum Daily 9 am-5 pm Historic museum interpreting sequoias, meadows, and human history. Start here before Big Trees Trail. Big Trees Trail Park access; begin at the museum Accessible interpretive circuit around Round Meadow, approximately 0.75-1 mile. Allow about one hour. General Sherman Tree and Congress Trail Park access; main lot and Wolverton Road open Highest-priority grove experience. The main approach descends a half mile; one Congress Trail section is under reconstruction through September, so confirm the signed route. Moro Rock Park access; Moro Rock Loop open Stair climb gaining about 300 feet to Great Western Divide views. Avoid rain, ice, lightning, and poor visibility. Tunnel Log and Crescent Meadow Park access; Crescent Meadow Road open Combine the quick Tunnel Log photo stop with the meadow and nearby sequoia trails. Beetle Rock Park access; short walk from the museum Broad granite viewpoint and an easy addition before or after the museum. Grant Grove Site or attraction Hours and access Why go and current notes Kings Canyon Visitor Center Daily 8 am-5 pm The visitor center at Grant Grove. Confirm Highway 180 and Cedar Grove conditions before the canyon drive. General Grant Tree Park access; Grant Grove trails open Paved one-third-mile loop with the General Grant Tree, Gamlin Cabin, Fallen Monarch, and Centennial Stump. Panoramic Point Park access; road open to passenger vehicles Views across Kings Canyon and Hume Lake. The road is narrow and prohibits motor homes and trailers. Kings Canyon Scenic Byway and Cedar Grove Site or attraction Hours and access Why go and current notes Kings Canyon Scenic Byway Highway 180 open to Roads End Dedicated driving day. Allow 45-60 minutes each way just for the Grant Grove-to-Cedar Grove descent, before stops. Junction View, Yucca Point, and Canyon View Park access; roadside overlooks Prioritize Junction View and Canyon View; add Yucca Point if pullout conditions are comfortable. Grizzly Falls Park access; five-minute roadside walk Shady, high-value waterfall stop with little time cost. Roaring River Falls Park access; short paved walk Granite-chute waterfall three miles east of Cedar Grove Village. Zumwalt Meadow Park access; trail reported open Approximately 0.8-mile current route with meadow, granite walls, talus, and river views. Flood damage ended the former loop. Knapp's Cabin Park access; short walk from a turnout Unusual 1920s fishing-expedition cabin and a quick human-history stop. Roads End and Muir Rock Highway 180 open to the terminus Granite-wall views, river access, and a worthwhile finish to the scenic byway when daylight permits. Closed or constrained Crystal Cave: tours have ended for the entire 2026 season. Remove it from the active itinerary. Shuttles: 2026 summer service ended September 7, and Kings Canyon has no in-park shuttle. Mineral King: major daytime construction closures make it a poor spontaneous backup. Parking: General Sherman and Giant Forest Museum lots can fill early, especially on weekends. Recheck roads , current conditions , and live alerts each morning. Trips markdown
